item.content:encoded:
Skimming the comments, it seems like the majority read the death of Mr. S as him being targeted by someone with a second uncontained zapper.

But the second addendum establishes that the other side of the screen has some level of reality, enough to affect this side at least sometimes.

So how about this: Mr. S shot up C-Span and created a militaristic, totalitarian alternative US in the "TV-verse". Which only he could see footage of, but the timeline was still running even when he wasn't watching the news. A high priority goal for that government would obviously be figuring out who shot up most of the prior administration, and how they managed it. Assume they got some insight from the TV-verse Foundation, either willingly or by annexing the organization, and it wouldn't take long to connect the dots with 674. The new powers that be not having our Foundation's reluctance to exploit anomalies, the TV-CIA pins down which alternate universe the shooter is in, confront him via the newly-constructed quark-based fourth-wall-drill, and proceed to remove the clear and present danger.

This, plus the implication that the more you use it, the more you corrupt the "rules" of what you are shooting at.

So yeah, you could kill every major character of a bland sitcom series or any show depicting normal life and get something new built around your interaction. The more you make the video reality aware of your presence, the more it fights back with whatever means at its disposal. Sometimes it does so by revealing information that will ultimately harm you, sometimes the Tazmanian Devil leaps out of your television and rips you apart, sometimes the video finds a way to reverse the rules by putting you on a reality show called "Shoot the Fat Bastard in the Holding Cell with No Cover (it'll be fun and easy)"

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
My feeling is that so long as the "rules of reality" of the show allow them to be aware of extradimensional effects, they can respond to the shooter. So, most Looney Tunes and Warner-Brothers cartoons regularly break the 4th wall, acknowledging and directly interacting with the "real world". So the cartoon was able to "see" the shooter and talk straight to him. Similarly, Star Trek regularly technobabbles about using weird science to defeat unseen/unknown foes, including extradimensional ones. So even if they can't directly perceive the shooter, they can still respond.

This is also why shows (or live TV) that depict "normal" reality can't respond; there's no readily available tech in the "real world" that lets you interact with parallel dimensions.
